newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds likely to weaken, some curve steepening seen.
newsitem.headline: Bunds likely to weaken, some curve steepening seen.

text.p: German debt prices will take their lead from the U.S. this week, with several weighty data releases due to hit financial markets in the coming sessions.

Analysts said that after a dramatic flattening of the yield curve late last week on worries that the Bundesbank might shift to a varibale repo rate, the scope for curve steepening trades to be put back on to correct that move was relatively good.
"The short end of the yield curve finally got oversold enough to attract investors who believe this sector now represents value," said Karl Haeling at DMG Futures and Options in Frankfurt.
He said that a reasonable recovery at the short end on Friday suggested the outlook was better in this region, adding that the two-year DTB Schatz contract was also fairly oversold.
At the long end, however, any curve steepening activity this week will add pressure to prices, which are anyway likely to be led by the nose by the U.S. market, analysts said.

"Over the coming week, with (domestic) economic releases in scarce supply, the Bund market will be driven by two factors -- the Treasury market and currency movements," Daiwa analysts said in an outlook.
They said this combination would spell trouble for Bunds.
"We expect modest downside for the Treasury market as investors take stock after the recent bull run. This will have a double-edged impact on Bunds," they said.

Although weakness in Treasuries might serve to halt the rise of the dollar against the mark, the debt market weakness itself will drag Bunds lower, probably cancelling out any positive pull on the German market from a slowing in the mark's recent sharp decline.
By 0642 GMT, the mark was trading at around 1.8460 to the dollar, near it lowest levels for almost seven years.
By 0655 GMT, the 10-year benchmark cash Bund was trading at 103.12 for a bid yield of 5.573 percent with the 10-year yield gap to Treasuries at 71 basis points.

The DTB September future was at 102.72, down 18 basis points on the day, and looking for first support in the 102.62 region. Beyond there, 102.53, the low from July 21, would kick in to stem losses, analysts said.
In the Bobl, which was also 18 basis points lower at 104.88 by 0656 GMT, analysts said the first support region would emerge at 104.70.

The U.S. is due to release its employment cost index and comsumer sentiment data on Tuesday, followed by weekly joblesss claims, weekly money supply, the first reading of second quarter GDP, the second quarter price index and implicit deflator and the Chicago PMI on Thursday, topped on Friday with the July unemployment report, NAPM, personal income and personal spending data, factory orders and the Michigan survey.
Little wonder that Bunds will have limited scope for independent movement.
